title: Deploying AI Inside a Bank Is Not an Engineering Problem — Paden Gayle, Applied AI Engineers
talk_summary: A deployment engineer argues that shipping AI inside a bank is gated by organizational discovery (data owners, risk signers, audit evidence) rather than model or engineering quality. The transferable mechanisms are a week-one decision checklist, an autonomy ladder, and a per-run evidence pack that records inputs, model version, config, output, and reviewer action.

takeaways.what_they_do: For every evaluation/run they persist the input, prompt, model version, configuration, output, and the human reviewer's action, so a past decision can be reconstructed without re-calling the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: preserve the input prompts model version configuration output reviewer action that lets us reconstruct the historical decision

takeaways.technique: Segment results and lead with the weakest segment
takeaways.what_they_do: Split evaluation cases into groups (clean docs, scans, rare exceptions, new types), measure errors per group, and report the worst group first rather than an average.
takeaways.evidence_quote: An average can hide a serious gap in one segment.

takeaways.what_they_do: Start each workflow at the lowest authority that creates value (suggest → draft → act-with-approval → act), then grant more authority only when observed override/failure/recovery evidence supports it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I start with the least authority that the problem solved then ask what task can be proven as evidence to give the system more.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before committing to delivery, answer five named-owner questions (data owner engaged, prod admins named, workflow describable without 'AI', smallest scope fits existing controls, risk signer known) and use the score to decide whether to proceed, shrink, or resolve first.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Four or five yeses suggest a credible path to ship. Three means unresolved decisions need owners and dates.
takeaways.numbers: 0-5 scoring heuristic; 4-5 yes = credible path, 3 = needs owners/dates, 0-2 = resolve before committing

takeaways.technique: Name detection path, fallback, and owner per failure mode
takeaways.what_they_do: Enumerate failure modes (invented output, unreadable input, missed cases) and for each specify how it is detected, what the fallback is, and who owns it; keep affected work under manual review when detection is incomplete.
takeaways.evidence_quote: For each failure, name the detection path, the fallback, and its owner.
